questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Bretton Woods Conference that created the IMF and the World Bank was held in 1944 in the United States.
2. The IMF formally came into existence in 1945 after enough members ratified its Articles of Agreement.
3. The International Development Association lends at market rates mainly to middle-income countries.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 1944 conference at Bretton Woods set up both institutions, and the IMF came into being in December 1945. IDA is the World Bank's concessional arm for the poorest countries, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (International Economic Institutions chapter)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the World Bank Group:
1. The IBRD and the IDA together are commonly called the World Bank.
2. The International Finance Corporation lends to and invests in the private sector in developing countries.
3. The Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency provides political risk insurance and guarantees for investors.
4. The International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes is headquartered in Geneva.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. ICSID, which handles investor-state disputes, is part of the World Bank Group and is based in Washington DC.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (International Economic Institutions chapter)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Special Drawing Rights (SDRs):
1. SDR is an international reserve asset created by the IMF in 1969.
2. SDR is a currency issued by the IMF that can be used directly to pay for imports.
3. The SDR basket includes the Chinese renminbi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The SDR is a reserve asset and a potential claim on the freely usable currencies of IMF members, not a currency in itself. The renminbi joined the dollar, euro, yen and pound in the basket in 2016.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (International Economic Institutions chapter)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the World Trade Organization:
1. It came into existence on 1 January 1995 as the successor to the GATT system.
2. The Ministerial Conference, its highest decision-making body, meets at least once every two years.
3. Decisions are normally taken by weighted voting based on each member's share of world trade.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The WTO emerged from the Uruguay Round, and its ministerial conference meets at least every two years. It works by consensus with one member, one vote, not by weighted voting as in the IMF.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (WTO and International Trade chapter)

questions.q:
Statement-I: The WTO's Appellate Body has been unable to hear appeals since December 2019.
Statement-II: The United States has blocked the appointment of new Appellate Body members, leaving it without the minimum number of members needed to hear an appeal.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: Appointments to the Appellate Body need consensus, so one member's block was enough to leave it without a quorum. Panel rulings can then be appealed 'into the void', which weakens enforcement.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (WTO and International Trade chapter)

questions.q: In the WTO dispute settlement system, the Dispute Settlement Body adopts panel reports unless all members decide by consensus not to adopt them. This rule is known as
o: unanimity of the parties to the dispute
questions.e: Under reverse consensus a report is adopted unless every member, including the winner, rejects it. This made the panel stage almost automatic, unlike the GATT days when the losing party could block adoption.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (WTO and International Trade chapter)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the WTO Agreement on Agriculture:
1. Amber box subsidies are exempt from any reduction commitment.
2. Green box subsidies are those that are not trade-distorting or only minimally so.
3. Developing countries can give trade-distorting domestic support up to 10 percent of the value of production under the de minimis provision.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Amber box measures are the trade-distorting ones that are subject to reduction commitments. The de minimis limit is 10 percent for developing countries and 5 percent for developed countries.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (WTO and International Trade chapter)
questions.h: Amber is the warning colour: it must be cut.

questions.q:
Statement-I: At the Bali Ministerial Conference (2013), WTO members agreed on an interim 'peace clause' for public stockholding programmes of developing countries.
Statement-II: India's procurement of foodgrains at minimum support prices can exceed the subsidy limits because support is measured against fixed external reference prices of 1986-88.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Because the reference prices are decades old, administered prices in India look like subsidy even when inflation explains much of the gap. That is why India sought the peace clause to avoid legal challenge.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (WTO and International Trade chapter)

questions.q:
Match List-I (Decision or Agreement) with List-II (Ministerial Conference):
List-I
A. Trade Facilitation Agreement
B. Decision to eliminate agricultural export subsidies
C. Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies
D. Launch of the Doha Development Agenda
List-II
1. Doha (2001)
2. Bali (2013)
3. Nairobi (2015)
4. Geneva (2022)
questions.e: The Doha Round began in 2001, the TFA was concluded at Bali in 2013, the export subsidy decision came at Nairobi in 2015 and the fisheries agreement at Geneva in 2022.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (WTO and International Trade chapter)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding trade remedies under WTO rules:
1. Anti-dumping duty can be imposed on imports from specific countries found to be selling below normal value.
2. Safeguard measures can be taken only against imports from the particular countries found to be dumping.
3. Countervailing duty is imposed to offset subsidies given by the exporting country.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Dumping and subsidies are specific to exporters, so duties target them. Safeguards respond to a surge in imports and apply to all sources without discrimination, so statement 2 is wrong.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (WTO and International Trade chapter)

questions.q:
Statement-I: In India, the Directorate General of Trade Remedies directly imposes anti-dumping duties.
Statement-II: The DGTR conducts the investigation and recommends the duty, which is then imposed by the Central Government through the Ministry of Finance.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
questions.e: DGTR, in the Department of Commerce, is the investigating authority. The final duty is notified by the Department of Revenue in the Ministry of Finance, so Statement-I is incorrect.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (WTO and International Trade chapter)

questions.q: In 2018 the United States imposed tariffs on steel and aluminium imports on national security grounds under
o: Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act, 1962
questions.e: Section 232 allows tariffs where imports threaten national security. Section 301 deals with unfair trade practices of other countries and was used for the China tariffs in 2018.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (WTO and International Trade chapter)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM):
1. It requires importers of certain goods to account for the carbon emitted in producing them.
2. Its initial scope includes textiles and garments.
3. India has objected to it as being inconsistent with the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: CBAM puts a carbon price on imports of goods such as steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, electricity and hydrogen. Textiles are not in its initial scope, and India sees it as a unilateral trade barrier that ignores CBDR.
questions.s: UNFCCC; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Climate and Environment-related chapter)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indo-Pacific Economic Framework for Prosperity (IPEF):
1. It was launched in May 2022 with four pillars.
2. India joined the pillars on supply chains, clean economy and fair economy.
3. India joined the trade pillar from the beginning.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: IPEF has pillars on trade, supply chains, clean economy and fair economy. India joined the last three but stayed out of the trade pillar, seeking more clarity on labour and environment standards.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (WTO and International Trade chapter)

questions.q: The Supply Chain Resilience Initiative, launched in 2021, is a trilateral effort of India with
questions.e: India, Japan and Australia launched SCRI to reduce dependence on any single source in supply chains after the pandemic exposed concentration risk.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (WTO and International Trade chapter)

questions.q:
Match List-I (Term) with List-II (Meaning):
List-I
A. Reshoring
B. Near-shoring
C. Friend-shoring
D. China plus one
List-II
1. Bringing production back to the home country
2. Relocating production to a nearby country
3. Relocating supply chains to politically allied countries
4. Diversifying sourcing beyond China while retaining some presence there
questions.e: These are the main strategies firms and governments use to de-risk supply chains: bring home, move nearby, move to allies, or add alternatives to China.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (WTO and International Trade chapter)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC):
1. It was announced at the G20 Summit in New Delhi in 2023.
2. The MoU was signed by India, the United States, Saudi Arabia, the UAE and the European Union along with France, Germany and Italy.
3. It includes the Chabahar port in Iran.
4. It has an eastern corridor linking India with the Gulf and a northern corridor linking the Gulf with Europe.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Chabahar belongs to the International North-South Transport Corridor, not to IMEC.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (WTO and International Trade chapter)

questions.q: The International North-South Transport Corridor agreement of 2000 was originally signed by
o: India, the UAE and Saudi Arabia
questions.e: INSTC was conceived as a multimodal route linking India with Russia and Europe via Iran and the Caspian region, shortening transit time and cost compared with the Suez route.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (WTO and International Trade chapter)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the New Development Bank:
1. It was established in 2008 after the global financial crisis.
2. Its headquarters is in Shanghai.
3. Its first president was K. V. Kamath of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The BRICS countries signed the agreement for the NDB in 2014 and it began operating in 2015. It is based in Shanghai, with Kamath as its first president.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (International Economic Institutions chapter)

questions.q: In the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, the second largest shareholder after China is
questions.e: India holds the second largest voting share in AIIB, ahead of Russia. Japan, a major Asian economy, is not a member.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (International Economic Institutions chapter)

questions.q:
Statement-I: Several countries are exploring settlement of trade in local currencies as part of efforts to reduce dependence on the US dollar.
Statement-II: Dependence on one dominant reserve currency exposes countries to exchange rate shocks and to the risk of financial sanctions.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Sanctions and dollar liquidity shocks have shown the vulnerability of a single-currency system. That is the motive behind local-currency settlement arrangements.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (International Economic Institutions chapter)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Special Rupee Vostro Accounts (SRVA):
1. The RBI introduced a mechanism for international trade settlement in rupees in July 2022.
2. Rupee balances in SRVA must be repatriated immediately in US dollars.
3. Surplus balances in the account can be invested in Indian government securities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Authorised dealer banks open SRVAs for partner-country banks, and surplus balances can be parked in G-secs. There is no requirement to convert balances into dollars, which is the point of the mechanism.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (International Economic Institutions chapter)

questions.q: The 'Triffin dilemma' refers to the situation in which
o: a country cannot have a fixed exchange rate, free capital mobility and independent monetary policy together
the issuer of the global reserve currency must run external deficits to supply reserves, which erodes confidence in the currency
resource exports cause the currency to appreciate and hurt manufacturing
a depreciation first worsens the trade balance before improving it
questions.e: To supply the world with dollars, the US has to run deficits, but persistent deficits weaken trust in the currency. The other options describe the impossible trinity, Dutch disease and the J-curve.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (International Economic Institutions chapter)
questions.h: Triffin: deficits give liquidity but cost trust.

questions.q:
Arrange the following events in the international monetary system in chronological order:
1. Plaza Accord
2. Bretton Woods Conference
3. Jamaica Accords
4. US suspension of dollar convertibility into gold
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The sequence is Bretton Woods (1944), the Nixon suspension of gold convertibility (1971), the Jamaica Accords legalising floating rates (1976) and the Plaza Accord (1985).
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (International Economic Institutions chapter)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A technical recession is commonly defined as two consecutive quarters of decline in real GDP.
2. In the United States, the official dating of recessions is done by the National Bureau of Economic Research's committee.
3. In the United States, recessions are officially declared by the Federal Reserve.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Two quarters of falling output is the rule of thumb, while the NBER committee looks at a broader set of indicators to date US recessions. The Federal Reserve does not declare them.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (International Economic Institutions chapter)

questions.q:
Statement-I: Stagflation is a situation with high inflation along with high unemployment and sluggish output.
Statement-II: The oil price shocks of the 1970s are regarded as a classic example of a trigger for stagflation in advanced economies.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are true, but the second is only an example of how stagflation occurred, not the definition or cause that makes the first statement true.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (International Economic Institutions chapter)

questions.q: The 'Fragile Five' label, coined in 2013 for economies vulnerable to capital outflows when the US Federal Reserve hinted at tapering, included India along with Brazil, Indonesia, South Africa and
questions.e: The 2013 taper tantrum triggered outflows from emerging markets with large current account deficits and high inflation. The label was coined by Morgan Stanley.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (International Economic Institutions chapter)

questions.q: An inverted yield curve, which is often treated as a warning of a coming recession, occurs when
o: yields on long-term bonds are much higher than on short-term bonds
yields on all bonds fall to zero
bond prices rise only for corporate debt
yields on short-term government bonds are higher than yields on long-term bonds
questions.e: Investors accept lower long-term yields when they expect growth and policy rates to fall. A normal curve slopes upward because long-term lending carries more risk.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (International Economic Institutions chapter)

questions.q: In a liquidity trap, monetary policy becomes ineffective mainly because
o: people prefer to hold cash even when interest rates are very low
the central bank cannot print money
questions.e: When rates are close to zero, extra money supply is hoarded rather than spent or lent, so further easing does not raise demand. Keynes described this situation.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (International Economic Institutions chapter)

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Term : Meaning
1. Disinflation : A fall in the rate of inflation with prices still rising
2. Deflation : A fall in the general price level
3. Reflation : A sudden collapse of the price level
4. Stagflation : High growth with very low inflation
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. Reflation is policy-driven revival of prices and output after a slowdown, and stagflation is stagnant output with high inflation.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (International Economic Institutions chapter)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the G20:
1. It was formed in 2008 after the global financial crisis.
2. Leaders' summits began in 2008.
3. It has no permanent secretariat and its presidency rotates among members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The G20 began in 1999 as a forum of finance ministers and central bank governors after the Asian financial crisis, and leaders began meeting in 2008. It works without a permanent secretariat.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (International Economic Institutions chapter)

questions.q: At the New Delhi Summit of the G20 in 2023, which grouping was admitted as a permanent member?
questions.e: The African Union joined the G20 as a permanent member at the New Delhi Summit under India's presidency, on the same footing as the European Union.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (International Economic Institutions chapter)

questions.q: The Financial Stability Board, which coordinates financial regulation at the international level, was established by the
questions.e: After the global financial crisis the G20 expanded the earlier Financial Stability Forum into the FSB. It is hosted by the Bank for International Settlements in Basel.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (International Economic Institutions chapter)

questions.q: The headquarters of the Green Climate Fund is located at
questions.e: The GCF, set up under the UNFCCC in 2010, is based at Songdo, Incheon. Bonn hosts the UNFCCC secretariat and Washington hosts the Global Environment Facility.
questions.s: UNFCCC; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Climate and Environment-related chapter)

questions.q: At which Conference of the Parties did developed countries commit to jointly mobilise USD 100 billion a year by 2020 for climate action in developing countries?
questions.e: The goal came out of the 2009 Copenhagen conference. Paris later extended it to 2025 and called for a new collective goal beyond that.
questions.s: UNFCCC; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Climate and Environment-related chapter)

questions.q: The New Collective Quantified Goal on climate finance adopted at COP29 in Baku set a target for developed countries to take the lead in mobilising at least
o: USD 1.3 trillion per year by 2035 as a binding commitment
questions.e: COP29 set USD 300 billion a year by 2035 and called on all actors to scale up to USD 1.3 trillion, which is an aspiration rather than a binding target. India objected that the amount was too low.
questions.s: UNFCCC; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Climate and Environment-related chapter)

questions.q:
Arrange the following climate conferences in chronological order:
1. Paris (COP21)
2. Copenhagen (COP15)
3. Glasgow (COP26)
4. Baku (COP29)
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Copenhagen was 2009, Paris 2015, Glasgow 2021 and Baku 2024.
questions.s: UNFCCC; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Climate and Environment-related chapter)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding India's climate commitments:
1. India announced the target of net-zero emissions by 2070 at COP26 in Glasgow.
2. India's updated NDC aims to reduce the emissions intensity of its GDP by 45 percent by 2030 from the 2005 level.
3. India's updated NDC aims to cut absolute emissions by 45 percent by 2030.
4. At COP26 India announced a target of 500 GW of non-fossil energy capacity by 2030.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The 45 percent target is about emissions intensity per unit of GDP, not absolute emissions, which are still allowed to grow.
questions.s: UNFCCC; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Climate and Environment-related chapter)

questions.q: India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme has been notified under the
o: Energy Conservation Act, 2001, as amended in 2022
Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
questions.e: The 2022 amendment to the Energy Conservation Act enabled the carbon market. The scheme was notified in 2023.
questions.s: UNFCCC; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Climate and Environment-related chapter)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the International Solar Alliance:
1. It was launched at COP21 in Paris by India and France.
2. Its headquarters is in Gurugram, India.
3. Only countries lying between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn can become members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: ISA was launched in 2015 and is headquartered in Gurugram. Its Framework Agreement was amended in 2020 to allow all UN member states to join, so the tropical limit no longer applies.
questions.s: UNFCCC; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Climate and Environment-related chapter)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding regional economic integration:
1. Members of a customs union adopt a common external tariff.
2. Members of a free trade area adopt a common external tariff.
3. A common market allows free movement of labour and capital in addition to a customs union.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: In a free trade area each member keeps its own tariff on outsiders, which is why rules of origin are needed. A customs union adds a common external tariff and a common market adds factor mobility.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (WTO and International Trade chapter)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP):
1. India is a member of RCEP.
2. The United States is a member of RCEP.
3. RCEP came into force in January 2022.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: RCEP links ASEAN with China, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand. India walked out of the negotiations in November 2019 over market access and trade deficit concerns, and the US was never part of it.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (WTO and International Trade chapter)

questions.q: In the theory of customs unions, 'trade diversion' occurs when
o: imports shift from a lower-cost non-member to a higher-cost member because of preferential tariffs
imports shift from a higher-cost member to a lower-cost non-member after tariffs are removed
a country raises tariffs on all imports equally
exports of a country fall because of a currency appreciation
questions.e: The common external tariff makes a non-member's cheaper goods costlier, so buyers switch to a less efficient partner. This is the welfare cost, set against trade creation within the bloc.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (WTO and International Trade chapter)

questions.q: In free trade agreements, 'rules of origin' are primarily meant to
o: fix the common external tariff of the members
ensure that only goods genuinely produced in member countries receive preferential tariffs
set minimum wages for workers in member countries
decide the currency in which trade will be settled
questions.e: Without rules of origin, goods from a third country could enter through the member with the lowest tariff (trade deflection). Origin criteria such as regional value content or a change in tariff heading prevent this.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (WTO and International Trade chapter)

questions.q:
Match List-I (Report or Index) with List-II (Publishing Organisation):
List-I
A. Logistics Performance Index
B. Global Innovation Index
C. World Investment Report
D. Global Financial Stability Report
List-II
1. World Bank
2. World Intellectual Property Organization
3. UNCTAD
4. International Monetary Fund
questions.e: LPI is a World Bank index, GII comes from WIPO, the World Investment Report is from UNCTAD and the GFSR is an IMF flagship.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (International Economic Institutions chapter)

questions.q:
Statement-I: India has traditionally run a merchandise trade deficit but a surplus in services trade.
Statement-II: Strong exports of IT and business services, along with large inward remittances, offset part of the merchandise deficit in the current account.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: Software and business services exports and remittances are the main inflows under the invisibles account. They explain why the current account deficit is smaller than the trade deficit.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (International Economic Institutions chapter)

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a founding member of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) formed in 1960?
questions.e: The five founders at Baghdad were Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Venezuela. The UAE joined later, in 1967 through Abu Dhabi.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (International Economic Institutions chapter)

questions.q: According to the Marshall-Lerner condition, a currency depreciation improves the trade balance if
o: the sum of the price elasticities of demand for exports and imports is less than one
domestic inflation is lower than foreign inflation
the sum of the price elasticities of demand for exports and imports is greater than one
exports are invoiced in US dollars
questions.e: If demand responds strongly enough to price changes, the volume gains outweigh the higher import bill. When the sum is below one, the trade balance worsens, which is part of the J-curve story.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (International Economic Institutions chapter)

questions.q: In 2021 the World Bank discontinued which of the following publications after data irregularities were identified in its rankings?
questions.e: The Doing Business rankings were discontinued in September 2021 after concerns about data changes in some editions. The Bank later announced a new approach to assessing the business environment.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (International Economic Institutions chapter)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding principles of the WTO:
1. Under the Most Favoured Nation principle, a lower tariff given to one member can be given to another selectively.
2. National treatment requires imported goods, once they have entered the market, to be treated no less favourably than domestic goods.
3. WTO rules allow members to form free trade areas and customs unions subject to conditions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: MFN means any advantage given to one member must be extended to all, but GATT Article XXIV permits FTAs and customs unions if they cover substantially all trade. National treatment applies after goods enter the market.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (WTO and International Trade chapter)
